title: Testing a New Questionnaire: Experience of Receiving a Dementia Diagnosis
official: Testing the Psychometric Properties of a New Questionnaire Developed to Assess the Quality of a Dementia Diagnosis and the Association the Quality of the Dementia Diagnosis Has on Outcomes of Quality of Life and Wellbeing.
summary:
We've designed a new questionnaire to measure how well a dementia diagnosis is explained and shared with a person and their carer. The goal of this study is to check if this questionnaire works well (is reliable, valid, and easy to use). We also want to see if better-quality diagnosis conversations are linked to better wellbeing and quality of life.

Research questions:

* To test the psychometric properties of a newly developed measure assessing the quality of dementia diagnosis disclosure from the perspective of people with dementia and their care partners.
* To compare the association between the quality of the diagnosis and outcomes of quality of life depression, anxiety, resilience and post-traumatic stress.

Participants will:

* Complete the newly developed questionnaire alongside an established questionnaire of patient satisfaction and demographic details (stage one).
* Three months later they will complete four questionnaires on their quality of life and wellbeing (stage two).
* They can choose to complete an optional stage where they will complete the newly developed questionnaire 2 weeks after stage one.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Received a diagnosis of dementia within 6 months before enrolment
* Carers will need to have been present at the dementia diagnosis disclosure
* For carers to participate the person with dementia will need to consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Received a diagnosis of dementia more than 6 months before enrolment
* Carer who was not present at the dementia diagnosis disclosure
* Received a diagnosis of Mild Cognitive Impairment or Subjective Cognitive Impairment
* Not fluent in English
